# sec/waf — Web Application Firewall (Cloud Armor)

## What This Module Does
Configures Google Cloud Armor WAF policies with 18 security rules including OWASP protections and rate limiting.

## State
- **Backend**: GCS bucket `liftit-tf-state`, prefix `sec/waf`
- **Workspaces**: qa, staging, prod, sha, sec

## WAF Rules
| Priority | Action | Description | Status |
|----------|--------|-------------|--------|
| 1000 | allow | Trusted IPs whitelist | active |
| 1010 | deny(403) | Malicious user-agents (15 bots) | preview |
| 1020 | deny(403) | Stackdriver monitoring | preview |
| 1030 | deny(403) | SQL injection (sqli-v33-stable) | preview |
| 1040 | deny(403) | XSS (xss-v33-stable) | preview |
| 1050 | deny(403) | Local file inclusion | preview |
| 1060 | deny(403) | Remote code execution | preview |
| 1070 | deny(403) | Remote file inclusion | preview |
| 1080 | deny(403) | Method enforcement | preview |
| 1090 | deny(403) | Scanner detection | preview |
| 1100 | deny(403) | Protocol attacks | preview |
| 1110 | deny(403) | PHP attacks | preview |
| 1120 | deny(403) | Session fixation | preview |
| 1130 | deny(403) | Java attacks | preview |
| 1140 | deny(403) | NodeJS attacks | preview |
| 1150 | deny(403) | CVE vulnerabilities | preview |
| 1160 | deny(403) | SQLi in JSON | preview |
| 1170 | rate_based_ban | Rate limit (1000/min, ban at 2000/min for 5min) | preview |

## Outputs
- `waf_policy_name`

## Dependencies (remote state)
| Name | Prefix | Workspace | Provides |
|------|--------|-----------|----------|
| folders | `project` | gen | gcp_folder_id, gcp_projects_ids |
| dns | `networking/dns` | gen | zone IDs, API token |

## Providers
- Terraform `~> 1.14`, Google `~> 7.0`, Cloudflare `~> 4.0`

## Notes
Most rules are in **preview mode**. Switching to active requires testing to avoid false positives.

# Cloud Armor WAF Implementation

## What This Is

Implementation of Google Cloud Armor WAF policies across the Liftit GCP infrastructure. Centralizes a single WAF security policy in the `sec` project (security-454414) and attaches it to all 7 load balancers across environments, starting with QA. Includes endpoint analysis to prevent false positives before activation.

## Core Value

Protect all externally-exposed services from OWASP attacks and abuse without blocking legitimate traffic.

## Current Milestone: v1.0 Cloud Armor QA Rollout

**Goal:** Analyze all services behind load balancers, fine-tune WAF rules to prevent false positives, centralize the policy in sec, and attach it to QA load balancers.

**Target features:**
- Audit all services behind LBs for WAF compatibility (endpoints, payloads, patterns)
- Centralize WAF policy in sec project (single policy shared across all projects)
- Fine-tune WAF rules based on endpoint analysis (exclusions, sensitivity tuning)
- Attach WAF policy to all QA load balancers
- Transition rules from preview to active after validation

## Requirements

### Validated

<!-- Shipped and confirmed valuable. -->

- WAF policy module exists (`sec/waf/`) with 18 rules using preconfigured OWASP rule sets
- All 7 load balancers support `cloud_armor_policy` parameter (currently `null`)
- WAF module in tf-modules supports rules, rate limiting, and IP whitelisting

### Active

<!-- Current scope. Building toward these. -->

- [ ] Endpoint analysis for GKE services (35+ microservices)
- [ ] Endpoint analysis for frontend static sites (14+ GCS buckets)
- [ ] Endpoint analysis for VM-based apps (n8n/workflows, kutt/urlshortener, OSRM, inventarios, airflow, metabase, superset, wrenai, streamlit, sonar, monitor)
- [ ] Centralize WAF policy in sec workspace (cross-project reference)
- [ ] Fine-tune rules based on analysis (exclusions for known patterns)
- [ ] Attach WAF policy to all 7 QA load balancers
- [ ] Validate no false positives in QA

### Out of Scope

<!-- Explicit boundaries. Includes reasoning to prevent re-adding. -->

- Upgrading preconfigured rule versions (v33-stable to newer) — separate milestone after QA validation
- Staging/prod rollout — depends on QA success
- Custom WAF rules beyond OWASP preconfigs — focus on activating what exists first
- DDoS protection (Cloud Armor Adaptive Protection) — separate evaluation needed
- Bot management — current user-agent blocking is sufficient for v1

## Context

**Current WAF state:**
- Policy created per workspace with 18 rules (17 in preview, only IP whitelist active)
- NOT attached to any load balancer (`cloud_armor_policy = null` everywhere)
- Uses `google_compute_security_policy` + `google_compute_security_policy_rule`
- Rules: IP whitelist, user-agent blocking, SQLi, XSS, LFI, RCE, RFI, method enforcement, scanner detection, protocol attacks, PHP, session fixation, Java, NodeJS, CVE, JSON-SQLi, rate limiting

**Architecture change:**
- Current: One policy per workspace (qa, staging, prod, sha, sec)
- Target: Single centralized policy in sec project, referenced cross-project by all LBs

**Load balancers to protect (7 total):**
| Module | LB Name | Backend Type | Services | Workspace |
|--------|---------|-------------|----------|-----------|
| apps/gke | gke-apps | Zonal NEG | 35+ microservices | qa/staging/prod |
| apps/frontends | frontends | Backend bucket | 14+ static sites | qa/staging/prod |
| apps/airflow | airflow | Instance group | Airflow VM | qa/prod |
| apps/apps | apps-{ws} | Instance group | n8n, inventarios | qa/prod |
| common/apps | sha-apps | Instance group | kutt, sonar, OSRM, monitor | sha |
| bi/apps | bi-apps | Instance group | Metabase, Superset | bi |
| bi/wrenai-poc | wrenai-poc | Instance group | WrenAI, Streamlit | bi |

**High-risk services for false positives:**
- Keycloak (auth flows with complex tokens/cookies)
- Kong API Gateway (proxies all requests)
- TMS API (core business logic)
- Backoffice API (admin operations, possible SQL-like input)
- Excel-loader / LMS-excel-loader (file uploads)
- Docscan-service (document processing)
- Support-administration (Django admin with CSRF)
- Superset/Metabase (SQL query builders - will trigger SQLi rules)

## Constraints

- **Cross-project**: WAF policy in sec project must be referenceable from other projects (Cloud Armor policies are global per-project, need self_link)
- **Preview first**: All rules must remain in preview mode until false positive analysis is complete
- **QA only**: This milestone targets QA workspace only; staging/prod is separate milestone
- **No downtime**: Attaching policy in preview mode should have zero impact on traffic
- **Module compatibility**: Load balancer module already accepts `cloud_armor_policy` param

## Key Decisions

| Decision | Rationale | Outcome |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| Centralize WAF in sec project | Single policy to manage, consistent rules across envs | -- Pending |
| Start with QA | Lowest risk environment for testing | -- Pending |
| Analyze before activating | Avoid blocking legitimate traffic in production | -- Pending |
| Keep v33-stable rules | Upgrade is separate scope; focus on activation | -- Pending |
